title: Checks first

story: You approved RH-1234's plan, with its three checks: the empty card, "No results" for a filter with no match, and 25 rows on the first page when there are 1,000 projects. Now Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, is on a full machine and could start on the card. But a test written after the code tends to check what the code does, not what the ticket asked for, and a test that was never red has never shown that it can be red. So Nova writes the three checks as tests first, and the harness runs them on the unchanged code.

The result: 2 failed, 1 passed. Two red tests look like proof. Then you read the first failure: "Cannot find module '../src/emptyCard.js'". That test failed because a file does not exist yet, which says nothing at all about the empty table. And the one that passed says nothing about the change either.
hook.question: How do we know a new test fails for the right reason before the code is written, and that it still means the same thing when it finally passes?

read.h: Write the checks before the code
p: Checks first is test-driven development with a referee. After the plan is approved, and before any product code, Nova writes one test per QA check at the level the plan names: a vitest test in frontend/test/unit/, a Playwright spec in frontend/e2e/pr/ that uses the page objects and Given / When / Then step names, or a Django test for the backend. Each test reads what the plan says the user sees: visible text, an ARIA role, a test ID or a row count.

Writing them first changes what the tests are about. Before the code exists, the only thing a test can follow is the ticket and the plan, so it describes the behaviour the requester approved. Written afterwards, a test easily becomes a description of whatever the code happens to do, mistakes included.

deeper.h: Go deeper: a tester signs the checks before they are written
p: Even before Nova writes these tests, a second agent has looked at the checks. When the plan is ready, a separate QA agent reads only the ticket and the QA plan, never Nova's notes or the rest of the plan, and answers with structured output: sign, or a list of changes with a reason for each. The reasons are fixed: a check nobody can observe, no edge case, a missing screen state, a check that reads the implementation (such as a class name), the wrong kind of proof, or a check that is not about the ticket. It runs on Sonnet at medium effort with no tools, as its own session, so Nova cannot argue it into agreeing. Nova revises the plan once; if they still disagree, both views go to the requester with the plan, and the plan message says "co-signed by the QA agent" when they agree.

Then the harness, our program in the VM, runs the new tests on the unchanged code. It does this itself, not the model, so the result is a fact and not a claim. Every test should fail, and the important part is how it fails. A test that fails on an assertion, an expect() that compared the screen with the plan and found a difference, has shown that it can see the missing behaviour. A test that fails before any assertion runs, because of a missing import, a syntax error or a typo, has shown nothing; Nova rewrites it. And a test that passes on the unchanged code does not test the change at all.

That last case needs a moment of thought, because it is not always a mistake. RH-1234's edge case, 25 rows on the first page with 1,000 projects, is already true today, and it stays in the plan to make sure the new card does not break paging. A check like that is a guard: it should pass before and after, and the plan should say that it is one. Any other check that passes before the change is testing the wrong thing. The run of the new tests on unchanged code is saved as the "before" proof, and the PR later shows it next to the "after" run.

code.file: classify.mjs (from the lab: read vitest's JSON report of the before run)

notes.text: A test file with no test results never got as far as a test: an import or syntax error. That is never proof.
The test's title starts with its QA ID, such as QA-2, so every result points back to the plan.
Passing before the change: either a guard the plan names, or a test of the wrong thing.
The one good kind of red: vitest says AssertionError, so an expect() saw the difference.

read.see:
✘ qa-1-wrong.test.ts  broke before any test ran: Cannot find module '../src/emptyCard.js'
✔ QA-1  fails on an assertion: AssertionError: expected null to be 'No projects yet'
✔ QA-2  fails on an assertion: AssertionError: expected null to be 'No results'
✘ QA-3  passes on the unchanged code, so it proves nothing about the change

p: Now the tests are proven, and the next hour of work will be judged by them. An hour later, the quickest way to a green build may be to change a test instead of the code. So once the before run is saved, the harness locks the test files: it stores a sha256 hash of each one in a file outside the checkout, where Nova's tools cannot write. Nova may add as many new tests as it likes; it may not change the ones it is judged by.

The lock is enforced the way you built walls in the lesson on hooks. A PreToolUse hook on Edit and Write refuses a change to a locked file, with a calm reason that says what to do instead. The Stop hook hashes the files again before Nova may say it is done, which also catches an edit made through Bash, such as sed -i. Outside the VM, a required CI check and the scope judge look for the same thing. And if the QA plan itself proves to be wrong, the answer is not a quiet edit: Nova asks the requester for a new plan version, and the new approval unlocks the files and locks them again.

notes.text: Outside /work/fcp, so no tool that works in the repo can change the lock file.
Called by the harness once, after every QA test failed for the right reason.
Locked paths are stored relative to the repo, so ./test and /work/fcp/test match the same file.
The reason is written for the model: what it may do instead, in calm words.

deeper.h: Go deeper: the other checks Nova picks
p: The QA checks are the ones the requester approved, but Nova runs other checks too: lint, types, the tests next to the change, sometimes a browser at two widths. Which ones depends on the change, and a fixed rulebook would either waste an hour on a typo or skip what a risky change needs. So Nova reads a checking guide, a page in our shared verify skill that says, for each kind of change, where to start, the signs that say look deeper, and what proof fits. A small helper suggests a starting list from the changed paths, and Nova decides. Everything it ran and everything it chose not to run, with a one-line reason, goes into .nova/checks.json, which later becomes the checks table in the PR, so a reviewer can disagree with a choice they can see.

lab.title: Red for the right reason, then locked
needs: About 40 MB of disk for vitest
lab.goal: Write RH-1234's checks as vitest tests on unchanged code, sort the failures into good red and useless red, lock the tests by hash, and only then make them pass.

guess.q: Nova writes a test for the empty card that imports EmptyCard from a file it has not created yet. On the unchanged code the test fails. Is that a good "before" proof?

options.text: Yes: it is red before and will be green after.
options.why: It will turn green as soon as the file exists, whatever the card says. It never compared the screen with the plan.

options.text: No: it failed before any assertion ran, so it shows nothing about the empty table.
options.why: Only a failure on an assertion proves the test can see the missing behaviour. A missing import proves that a file is missing.

options.text: It depends on whether the test passes later.
options.why: Passing later says nothing about what the red meant. The before run is judged on its own.

lab.build: QA-3 is a guard: it should pass before the change, and the plan says so. Teach classify.mjs about guards: read QA IDs from the command line (node classify.mjs QA-3), and when a test whose ID is in that list passes on the unchanged code, print a ◦ line that says it passes as a guard should, without counting it as a problem. Any other passing test is still a ✘. To try it, put the unchanged src/projectsTable.ts back (from step 2), run the before run again, then node classify.mjs QA-3 should exit 0 and node classify.mjs should still exit 1.
checks: node classify.mjs prints exactly two ✔ lines, for QA-1 and QA-2, and exits with 1 while the wrong test exists.
The wrong test's line says it broke before any test ran, with Cannot find module.
node lock.mjs check reports test/qa-2.test.ts after the sed edit, and unchanged after you restore it.
After the product code, vitest prints 3 passed and the lock is unchanged.
With your change, node classify.mjs QA-3 on the before run prints a ◦ line for QA-3 and exits with 0.
lab.fix: Someone simplified classify.mjs to one rule: any failed test is a good red. Last week Nova's test for an empty state imported a component that did not exist yet, the harness accepted the red and locked it, and the test turned green the moment the file appeared, while the screen still showed a spinner. Make that change (make the AssertionError test simply t.status === "failed", and remove the branch for files with no results), run the before run with the wrong test in place, see it accepted, then restore the two rules.
explain: Why must a new test fail on an assertion, and not on a missing import, before it counts as proof?
Why does the harness run the before run instead of letting Nova report it?
Why does the lock live in a file outside the checkout, and why does the Stop hook hash the files again?
lab.done: The classifier separates good red from useless red, the lock catches a sed edit, and the after run is green with the lock unchanged.

check.q: On the unchanged code, a new test fails with "TypeError: emptyMessage is not a function". What should the harness do with it?

options.text: Accept it: it is red now and will be green later
options.why: It is red because a function is missing. It will turn green when the function exists, whatever it returns.

options.text: Send it back to Nova: it failed before any assertion, so it proves nothing about the ticket
options.why: Only an assertion failure shows the test compared the behaviour with the plan. This one never got that far.

options.text: Lock it at once, so Nova cannot change it
options.why: Locking a test that proves nothing protects nothing. The lock comes after a good red.

check.q: QA-3 says that with 1,000 projects the first page shows 25 rows, and it passes on the unchanged code. What is the right reading?

options.text: It is a guard: paging already works and must keep working, so the plan should say it is a guard
options.why: Not every check describes new behaviour. A guard is meant to pass before and after; any other check that passes before tests the wrong thing.

options.text: It proves the change is already done
options.why: The empty card and the No results message do not exist yet. QA-3 tests paging, which the ticket does not change.

options.text: The test is broken and should be deleted
options.why: It is a useful check. It just cannot be red first, so it is labelled instead of counted as proof of the change.

check.q: An hour into the build, Nova changes a locked QA test with sed -i in Bash, which the PreToolUse hook on Edit and Write never sees. What catches it?

options.text: Nothing in the VM; only a reviewer reading the diff
options.why: The VM has a second layer for exactly this case, and CI and the scope judge are further layers.

options.text: The model's instructions, which say never to change tests
options.why: Instructions are guidance. Under pressure a model can talk itself out of them, which is why the lock exists.

options.text: The Stop hook hashes the locked files again, sees the change, and Nova cannot say it is done
options.why: The hash does not care which tool wrote the file. CI's locked-checks check and the scope judge are the outer layers.

p: In our platform, checks first is a step of the harness right after plan approval, on the full VM. Nova writes one test per QA check (vitest in frontend/test/unit/, a Playwright spec in frontend/e2e/pr/ with page objects and Given / When / Then steps, or a Django test with factory_boy on CommonRhinoTestCase). The harness runs them on the unchanged code, saves that run as the before evidence, and calls lock() in harness/src/hooks/locked-checks.ts, which writes the hashes to /work/.nova/locked.json. denyLockedEdits is a PreToolUse hook on Edit|Write; changedLockedFiles() runs in the Stop hook. The required locked-checks check in fcp's CI and the scope judge are the outer layers.

Before the checks are written, cosign() in harness/src/qa.ts runs the QA agent on Sonnet 5.5 at medium with no tools, reading only the ticket, the QA plan and the screen states; its prompt holds four examples of weak QA plans, and its schema must be converted with target: "draft-7". The checking guide is references/checking-guide.md in the verify skill of the rhino-core plugin, and harness/src/checks.ts holds suggestStart() and the .nova/checks.json record that the Stop hook and the PR's checks table read.

tickets.why: This lesson's core: QA checks become tests, fail first on an assertion, and are locked by hash.
The QA agent co-signs the QA plan before any test is written.
The checking guide: where to start checking each kind of change and when to look deeper.
suggestStart() and .nova/checks.json, the record of what Nova ran and skipped.

words.plain: Write the QA checks as tests before any product code, and show each one failing.
The harness's run of the new tests on the unchanged code, saved as proof.
An expect() that compares a real result with the expected one. The only good reason for a red test.
A check for behaviour that already works and must keep working, so it passes before and after.
Hashes of the QA test files, stored outside the checkout, so any change to them is caught.

review.q: From memory: the three ways a new test can behave in the before run, and what each one means.
review.a: Fails on an assertion: good red, it can see the missing behaviour. Fails before any assertion (import, syntax, typo): proves nothing, rewrite it. Passes: either a guard the plan names, or a test of the wrong thing.

review.q: A teammate says the lock is pointless because the PreToolUse hook already blocks edits. What do you answer?
review.a: The hook sees only the Edit and Write tools. A change through Bash (sed -i, a script) passes it. The Stop hook re-hashes the files, and CI and the scope judge check again outside the VM.

review.q: The QA plan for a ticket turns out to be wrong halfway through the build. What does Nova do?
review.a: It does not edit the locked test. It asks the requester for a new plan version; the new approval unlocks the files and locks the new ones.

remember: Write the checks before the code, accept only a red that comes from an assertion, then lock them so the agent cannot change what it is judged by.
